column1: 3:47 AM. The screaming woke you.
en: 3:47 AM. The screaming woke you.
pt_BR: 3h47 da manhã. Os gritos te acordaram.

column1: Not the neighbors fighting again. Something worse. Something that doesn't sound human.
en: Not the neighbors fighting again. Something worse. Something that doesn't sound human.
pt_BR: Não era a briga dos vizinhos de novo. Algo pior. Algo que não soa humano.

column1: Your phone buzzes. A message from Marcus: 'Don't open the door. Don't go outside. They're everywhere.'
en: Your phone buzzes. A message from Marcus: 'Don't open the door. Don't go outside. They're everywhere.'
pt_BR: Seu celular vibra. Uma mensagem de Marcus: 'Não abra a porta. Não saia. Eles estão por toda parte.'

column1: Someone is banging on your apartment door. The sound is desperate. Human. You think.
en: Someone is banging on your apartment door. The sound is desperate. Human. You think.
pt_BR: Alguém bate com força na porta do seu apartamento. O som é desesperado. Humano. Você acha.

column1: Please! Please open the door! They're coming! I can hear them on the stairs!
en: Please! Please open the door! They're coming! I can hear them on the stairs!
pt_BR: Por favor! Por favor, abra a porta! Eles estão vindo! Posso ouvi-los na escada!

column1: Open the door — let them in
en: Open the door — let them in
pt_BR: Abrir a porta — deixá-la entrar

column1: Stay quiet — don't answer
en: Stay quiet — don't answer
pt_BR: Ficar em silêncio — não responder

column1: Look through the peephole first
en: Look through the peephole first
pt_BR: Olhar pelo olho mágico primeiro

column1: You throw the lock. The door flies open and a woman crashes into your arms, shaking.
en: You throw the lock. The door flies open and a woman crashes into your arms, shaking.
pt_BR: Você arranca o trinco. A porta se escancara e uma mulher desaba nos seus braços, tremendo.

column1: Thank god. Thank you. I thought... I saw them take Henderson down the hall. They just... they bit into him and he...
en: Thank god. Thank you. I thought... I saw them take Henderson down the hall. They just... they bit into him and he...
pt_BR: Graças a Deus. Obrigada. Eu pensei... eu vi eles pegarem o Henderson no corredor. Eles simplesmente... morderam ele e...

column1: We need to leave. The building. They're working through floor by floor.
en: We need to leave. The building. They're working through floor by floor.
pt_BR: Precisamos sair. Do prédio. Eles estão avançando andar por andar.

column1: You press your back against the wall and hold your breath.
en: You press your back against the wall and hold your breath.
pt_BR: Você comprime as costas contra a parede e prende a respiração.

column1: The banging stops. Then a sound you'll never forget — wet, tearing, and the voice that was begging goes silent.
en: The banging stops. Then a sound you'll never forget — wet, tearing, and the voice that was begging goes silent.
pt_BR: As batidas param. Então, um som que você nunca vai esquecer — úmido, rasgado, e a voz que implorava silencia.

column1: Minutes pass. Something drags itself away from your door. You're alone.
en: Minutes pass. Something drags itself away from your door. You're alone.
pt_BR: Minutos passam. Algo se arrasta para longe da sua porta. Você está sozinho.

column1: You press your eye to the peephole. A woman in her thirties, pajamas, barefoot. Behind her, something is crawling on the ceiling of the hallway.
en: You press your eye to the peephole. A woman in her thirties, pajamas, barefoot. Behind her, something is crawling on the ceiling of the hallway.
pt_BR: Você encosta o olho no olho mágico. Uma mulher de uns trinta anos, de pijama, descalça. Atrás dela, algo rasteja no teto do corredor.

column1: It has Henderson's face. But its joints bend the wrong way. And it's smiling.
en: It has Henderson's face. But its joints bend the wrong way. And it's smiling.
pt_BR: Tem o rosto do Henderson. Mas as juntas dobram para o lado errado. E está sorrindo.

column1: The woman hasn't seen it yet. It's three meters behind her. You have seconds.
en: The woman hasn't seen it yet. It's three meters behind her. You have seconds.
pt_BR: A mulher ainda não o viu. Está a três metros atrás dela. Você tem segundos.

column1: Yell through the door — 'GET DOWN!'
en: Yell through the door — 'GET DOWN!'
pt_BR: Gritar pela porta — 'ABAIXE!'

column1: Throw the door open and pull her inside
en: Throw the door open and pull her inside
pt_BR: Escancarar a porta e puxá-la para dentro

column1: Watch. Say nothing.
en: Watch. Say nothing.
pt_BR: Observar. Não dizer nada.

column1: The thing on the ceiling lunges. Elena throws herself through your doorway as you slam the door shut.
en: The thing on the ceiling lunges. Elena throws herself through your doorway as you slam the door shut.
pt_BR: A coisa no teto avança. Elena se joga pela sua porta enquanto você a bate com força.

column1: Something hits the other side. Once. Twice. Then it moves on.
en: Something hits the other side. Once. Twice. Then it moves on.
pt_BR: Algo bate do outro lado. Uma vez. Duas. Então segue em frente.

column1: What... what WAS that? That was Henderson. I've lived next to him for two years. That was Henderson.
en: What... what WAS that? That was Henderson. I've lived next to him for two years. That was Henderson.
pt_BR: O que... o que ERA aquilo? Aquilo era o Henderson. Eu morei ao lado dele por dois anos. Aquilo era o Henderson.

column1: Your apartment is on the 7th floor. The fire escape leads to the alley. The elevator is a death trap. The stairs... you heard something on them.
en: Your apartment is on the 7th floor. The fire escape leads to the alley. The elevator is a death trap. The stairs... you heard something on them.
pt_BR: Seu apartamento é no 7º andar. A escada de incêndio leva ao beco. O elevador é uma armadilha mortal. As escadas... você ouviu algo nelas.

column1: [Marcus]: I'm on the 4th floor. I have a car in the garage. Get to me and we go. NOW.
en: [Marcus]: I'm on the 4th floor. I have a car in the garage. Get to me and we go. NOW.
pt_BR: [Marcus]: Estou no 4º andar. Tenho um carro na garagem. Chegue até mim e vamos embora. AGORA.

column1: Take the fire escape down
en: Take the fire escape down
pt_BR: Descer pela escada de incêndio

column1: Risk the stairwell to reach Marcus
en: Risk the stairwell to reach Marcus
pt_BR: Arriscar a escada para chegar ao Marcus

column1: Barricade here and wait for sunrise
en: Barricade here and wait for sunrise
pt_BR: Fazer uma barricada e esperar o amanhecer

column1: The fire escape groans under your weight. Seven floors of rusted metal and the sounds of the city tearing itself apart below.
en: The fire escape groans under your weight. Seven floors of rusted metal and the sounds of the city tearing itself apart below.
pt_BR: A escada de incêndio range sob o seu peso. Sete andares de metal enferrujado e os sons da cidade se despedaçando lá embaixo.

column1: Halfway down, you see a supply bag on the 4th floor landing. Marcus's floor.
en: Halfway down, you see a supply bag on the 4th floor landing. Marcus's floor.
pt_BR: Na metade do caminho, você vê uma mochila de suprimentos no patamar do 4º andar. O andar do Marcus.

column1: The stairwell is dark. Emergency lights flicker. On the 6th floor landing, blood drags in a long smear down the stairs.
en: The stairwell is dark. Emergency lights flicker. On the 6th floor landing, blood drags in a long smear down the stairs.
pt_BR: A escada está escura. Luzes de emergência piscam. No patamar do 6º andar, sangue se arrasta numa longa mancha escada abaixo.

column1: You hear something breathing on the 5th floor. It's not human breathing.
en: You hear something breathing on the 5th floor. It's not human breathing.
pt_BR: Você ouve algo respirando no 5º andar. Não é uma respiração humana.

column1: You push the couch against the door. Wedge a chair under the knob. It won't hold forever, but maybe until morning.
en: You push the couch against the door. Wedge a chair under the knob. It won't hold forever, but maybe until morning.
pt_BR: Você empurra o sofá contra a porta. Encunha uma cadeira sob a maçaneta. Não vai aguentar para sempre, mas talvez até de manhã.

column1: Hours pass. The sounds outside get worse. Then, silence. The worst kind.
en: Hours pass. The sounds outside get worse. Then, silence. The worst kind.
pt_BR: Horas passam. Os sons lá fora pioram. Então, silêncio. O pior tipo.

column1: At dawn, you hear a voice in the hallway. Marcus. He sounds wrong. 'Let me in,' he says. 'I made it. Open up.'
en: At dawn, you hear a voice in the hallway. Marcus. He sounds wrong. 'Let me in,' he says. 'I made it. Open up.'
pt_BR: Ao amanhecer, você ouve uma voz no corredor. Marcus. Ele soa errado. 'Deixa eu entrar', ele diz. 'Eu consegui. Abre.'

column1: Marcus's voice. But you've known Marcus for five years. That cadence is off. He's speaking too slowly. Too carefully. Like he's reading lines.
en: Marcus's voice. But you've known Marcus for five years. That cadence is off. He's speaking too slowly. Too carefully. Like he's reading lines.
pt_BR: A voz do Marcus. Mas você conhece o Marcus há cinco anos. O ritmo está errado. Ele fala devagar demais. Cuidadoso demais. Como quem está lendo um roteiro.

column1: Come on, open the door. It's me. I'm fine. I'm totally fine. I just need to come in. Please.
en: Come on, open the door. It's me. I'm fine. I'm totally fine. I just need to come in. Please.
pt_BR: Vamos, abre a porta. Sou eu. Estou bem. Estou totalmente bem. Só preciso entrar. Por favor.

column1: Open the door for Marcus
en: Open the door for Marcus
pt_BR: Abrir a porta para o Marcus

column1: Tell Marcus to slide his ID under the door
en: Tell Marcus to slide his ID under the door
pt_BR: Pedir ao Marcus para deslizar o documento sob a porta

column1: Stay silent. Don't respond.
en: Stay silent. Don't respond.
pt_BR: Ficar em silêncio. Não responder.

column1: You move the couch. The door swings open. Marcus is standing there, smiling. His eyes are milk-white. The bite mark on his neck is still bleeding.
en: You move the couch. The door swings open. Marcus is standing there, smiling. His eyes are milk-white. The bite mark on his neck is still bleeding.
pt_BR: Você afasta o sofá. A porta se abre. Marcus está parado ali, sorrindo. Os olhos são brancos como leite. A marca de mordida no pescoço ainda sangra.

column1: He lunges.
en: He lunges.
pt_BR: Ele avança.

column1: You ask him to slide his ID under the door. There's a long pause.
en: You ask him to slide his ID under the door. There's a long pause.
pt_BR: Você pede que ele deslize o documento sob a porta. Há uma longa pausa.

column1: Then the sound of something heavy hitting the wall. A guttural, inhuman shriek. And then running. Down the stairs. Away.
en: Then the sound of something heavy hitting the wall. A guttural, inhuman shriek. And then running. Down the stairs. Away.
pt_BR: Então, o som de algo pesado batendo na parede. Um grito gutural, inumano. E depois passos correndo. Escada abaixo. Para longe.

column1: That wasn't Marcus.
en: That wasn't Marcus.
pt_BR: Aquele não era o Marcus.

column1: You say nothing. The voice outside repeats itself. Slower. Then it makes a sound — not a word. Something between a growl and a laugh.
en: You say nothing. The voice outside repeats itself. Slower. Then it makes a sound — not a word. Something between a growl and a laugh.
pt_BR: Você não diz nada. A voz lá fora se repete. Mais devagar. Então faz um som — não é uma palavra. Algo entre um rosnado e uma risada.

column1: It leaves. You hear it descend the stairwell, each step heavier than the last.
en: It leaves. You hear it descend the stairwell, each step heavier than the last.
pt_BR: Ele vai embora. Você o ouve descer a escada, cada passo mais pesado que o anterior.

column1: Dawn breaks gray and ugly over the city. From your window, you can see fires. Cars abandoned in the street. Figures moving wrong in the distance.
en: Dawn breaks gray and ugly over the city. From your window, you can see fires. Cars abandoned in the street. Figures moving wrong in the distance.
pt_BR: O amanhecer rompe cinza e feio sobre a cidade. Da sua janela, você vê incêndios. Carros abandonados na rua. Figuras se movendo de forma errada ao longe.

column1: Marcus's last message, from hours ago: 'If you get this, I'm already gone. The keys to the truck are under the visor. Get out of the city. Don't stop.'
en: Marcus's last message, from hours ago: 'If you get this, I'm already gone. The keys to the truck are under the visor. Get out of the city. Don't stop.'
pt_BR: A última mensagem do Marcus, de horas atrás: 'Se você está lendo isso, eu já era. As chaves do caminhão estão sob o para-sol. Saia da cidade. Não pare.'

column1: You make it to the parking garage. Marcus's truck is there. Keys under the visor, just like he said.
en: You make it to the parking garage. Marcus's truck is there. Keys under the visor, just like he said.
pt_BR: Você chega à garagem. O caminhão do Marcus está lá. Chaves sob o para-sol, como ele disse.

column1: But someone is already at the truck. A teenager, maybe sixteen. Blood on his shirt. A bite on his arm, fresh. He sees you.
en: But someone is already at the truck. A teenager, maybe sixteen. Blood on his shirt. A bite on his arm, fresh. He sees you.
pt_BR: Mas alguém já está no caminhão. Um adolescente, uns dezesseis anos. Sangue na camiseta. Uma mordida no braço, fresca. Ele te vê.

column1: Please. I stole this from a dead guy. I didn't know whose it was. Take it. I don't care. Just — can I come with you? I can't stay here.
en: Please. I stole this from a dead guy. I didn't know whose it was. Take it. I don't care. Just — can I come with you? I can't stay here.
pt_BR: Por favor. Eu roubei isso de um cara morto. Não sabia de quem era. Fica com ele. Não me importo. Só — posso ir com você? Eu não posso ficar aqui.

column1: Take the kid with you
en: Take the kid with you
pt_BR: Levar o garoto com você

column1: Take the truck, leave the kid
en: Take the truck, leave the kid
pt_BR: Ficar com o caminhão, deixar o garoto

column1: Ask about the bite before deciding
en: Ask about the bite before deciding
pt_BR: Perguntar sobre a mordida antes de decidir

column1: You ask about the bite. He looks at it like he forgot it was there.
en: You ask about the bite. He looks at it like he forgot it was there.
pt_BR: Você pergunta sobre a mordida. Ele olha para ela como se tivesse esquecido que estava ali.

column1: It's... I don't know. My dog bit me? It was my dog. He went crazy this morning and I—
en: It's... I don't know. My dog bit me? It was my dog. He went crazy this morning and I—
pt_BR: É... sei lá. Meu cachorro me mordeu? Era meu cachorro. Ele enlouqueceu hoje de manhã e eu—

column1: It doesn't matter. Please. I can help. I know how to drive. I know the city. Don't leave me here.
en: It doesn't matter. Please. I can help. I know how to drive. I know the city. Don't leave me here.
pt_BR: Não importa. Por favor. Posso ajudar. Sei dirigir. Conheço a cidade. Não me deixa aqui.

column1: The bite looks wrong. The skin around it is turning gray. You've seen enough horror movies. But he's a kid.
en: The bite looks wrong. The skin around it is turning gray. You've seen enough horror movies. But he's a kid.
pt_BR: A mordida parece errada. A pele ao redor está ficando cinza. Você já viu filmes de terror suficientes. Mas ele é um garoto.

column1: Take him. You can figure it out later.
en: Take him. You can figure it out later.
pt_BR: Levá-lo. Você resolve isso depois.

column1: Tie off the wound and take him — but watch him
en: Tie off the wound and take him — but watch him
pt_BR: Façar o ferimento e levá-lo — mas fique de olho

column1: Tell him the truth — you can't risk it
en: Tell him the truth — you can't risk it
pt_BR: Dizer a verdade — você não pode arriscar

column1: Thank you. I swear I won't be a problem. I know the back roads out of the city. My dad taught me before he...
en: Thank you. I swear I won't be a problem. I know the back roads out of the city. My dad taught me before he...
pt_BR: Obrigado. Juro que não vou dar problema. Conheço as estradas secundárias para sair da cidade. Meu pai me ensinou antes de...

column1: There's a gas station on Route 9. We can stock up there.
en: There's a gas station on Route 9. We can stock up there.
pt_BR: Tem um posto de gasolina na Estrada 9. Podemos nos abastecer lá.

column1: Yeah. Yeah, I get it. I'd leave me too.
en: Yeah. Yeah, I get it. I'd leave me too.
pt_BR: É. É, eu entendo. Eu também me deixaria.

column1: You get in the truck. In the mirror, the kid sits on the curb. He doesn't move. He doesn't watch you go.
en: You get in the truck. In the mirror, the kid sits on the curb. He doesn't move. He doesn't watch you go.
pt_BR: Você entra no caminhão. No retrovisor, o garoto senta na calçada. Ele não se move. Não vê você partir.

column1: You don't know how long a bite takes. You don't know if you just killed him or saved yourself.
en: You don't know how long a bite takes. You don't know if you just killed him or saved yourself.
pt_BR: Você não sabe quanto tempo uma mordida leva. Não sabe se acabou de matá-lo ou de se salvar.

column1: The city burns behind you. The highway is empty. Whatever you did tonight — who you saved, who you left, who you let in — it's with you now.
en: The city burns behind you. The highway is empty. Whatever you did tonight — who you saved, who you left, who you let in — it's with you now.
pt_BR: A cidade queima atrás de você. A rodovia está vazia. O que quer que você tenha feito esta noite — quem salvou, quem deixou, quem deixou entrar — está com você agora.

column1: The dead don't forget. And neither does the kid in your backseat. If he's there.
en: The dead don't forget. And neither does the kid in your backseat. If he's there.
pt_BR: Os mortos não esquecem. E o garoto no banco de trás também não. Se ele estiver lá.

column1: Route 9. The gas station sits alone in a sea of dead grass. The lights are on. That should be reassuring. It isn't.
en: Route 9. The gas station sits alone in a sea of dead grass. The lights are on. That should be reassuring. It isn't.
pt_BR: Estrada 9. O posto de gasolina fica sozinho num mar de grama morta. As luzes estão acesas. Isso deveria tranquilizar. Não tranquiliza.

column1: There's a group inside. You can see them through the windows. Four, maybe five people. They have guns.
en: There's a group inside. You can see them through the windows. Four, maybe five people. They have guns.
pt_BR: Tem um grupo lá dentro. Você os vê pelas janelas. Quatro, talvez cinco pessoas. Eles têm armas.

column1: A man steps out the front door. Shotgun, low and ready. Not pointed at you. Not pointed away either.
en: A man steps out the front door. Shotgun, low and ready. Not pointed at you. Not pointed away either.
pt_BR: Um homem sai pela porta da frente. Espingarda, baixa e pronta. Não apontada para você. Nem apontada para longe.

column1: That's far enough. How many in the vehicle? Any bites?
en: That's far enough. How many in the vehicle? Any bites?
pt_BR: Aí é longe o suficiente. Quantos no veículo? Alguma mordida?

column1: Tell the truth about your group
en: Tell the truth about your group
pt_BR: Dizer a verdade sobre o seu grupo

column1: Lie — say it's just you, no bites
en: Lie — say it's just you, no bites
pt_BR: Mentir — dizer que é só você, sem mordidas

column1: Wait for nightfall, sneak in for supplies
en: Wait for nightfall, sneak in for supplies
pt_BR: Esperar anoitecer, entrar escondido para pegar suprimentos

column1: Honest. I respect that. Most people lie.
en: Honest. I respect that. Most people lie.
pt_BR: Honesto. Respeito isso. A maioria mente.

column1: The kid with the bite stays outside. I don't care if it's a dog bite or a zombie bite. Outside. That's the deal.
en: The kid with the bite stays outside. I don't care if it's a dog bite or a zombie bite. Outside. That's the deal.
pt_BR: O garoto com a mordida fica lá fora. Não me interessa se é mordida de cachorro ou de zumbi. Lá fora. Esse é o trato.

column1: Just you. Alright. Come in. But I'm watching.
en: Just you. Alright. Come in. But I'm watching.
pt_BR: Só você. Tudo bem. Entre. Mas estou de olho.

column1: Garcia's eyes linger on Danny a beat too long. He might know. Or he might just be careful. Either way, you're inside.
en: Garcia's eyes linger on Danny a beat too long. He might know. Or he might just be careful. Either way, you're inside.
pt_BR: Os olhos de Garcia demoram um segundo a mais em Danny. Ele pode saber. Ou pode só ser cuidadoso. De qualquer forma, você está dentro.

column1: You wait. Hours. The sun drops. The group inside settles into watches. The back door has a padlock you can pick.
en: You wait. Hours. The sun drops. The group inside settles into watches. The back door has a padlock you can pick.
pt_BR: Você espera. Horas. O sol se põe. O grupo lá dentro se organiza nos turnos de vigília. A porta dos fundos tem um cadeado que você sabe arrombar.

column1: You slip in through the back. Aisle three. The shelves are still half-stocked.
en: You slip in through the back. Aisle three. The shelves are still half-stocked.
pt_BR: Você entra pelos fundos. Corredor três. As prateleiras ainda estão meio abastecidas.

column1: A flashlight hits your face. A woman, rifle aimed at your chest.
en: A flashlight hits your face. A woman, rifle aimed at your chest.
pt_BR: Uma lanterna acerta seu rosto. Uma mulher, rifle apontado para o seu peito.

column1: Don't move. Don't even breathe wrong. Garcia! We've got a thief.
en: Don't move. Don't even breathe wrong. Garcia! We've got a thief.
pt_BR: Não se move. Nem respire errado. Garcia! Temos um ladrão.

column1: Drop to your knees and surrender
en: Drop to your knees and surrender
pt_BR: Ajoelhar e se entregar

column1: Grab what you can and run
en: Grab what you can and run
pt_BR: Pegar o que puder e correr

column1: You shove the shelf. Bottles crash. You sprint for the back door with a bag of supplies.
en: You shove the shelf. Bottles crash. You sprint for the back door with a bag of supplies.
pt_BR: Você empurra a prateleira. Garrafas se estilhaçam. Você dispara para a porta dos fundos com um saco de suprimentos.

column1: A shot rings out. Glass shatters above your head. You make it to the truck. Danny is screaming. You drive.
en: A shot rings out. Glass shatters above your head. You make it to the truck. Danny is screaming. You drive.
pt_BR: Um tiro ecoa. Vidro se estilhaça acima da sua cabeça. Você chega ao caminhão. Danny está gritando. Você dirige.

column1: They'll remember you. And you just made enemies on a road with nowhere to hide.
en: They'll remember you. And you just made enemies on a road with nowhere to hide.
pt_BR: Eles vão lembrar de você. E você acabou de fazer inimigos numa estrada sem lugar para se esconder.

column1: We've been here three days. Military radio went dead yesterday. Last transmission said there's a safe zone — Riverside, forty miles north.
en: We've been here three days. Military radio went dead yesterday. Last transmission said there's a safe zone — Riverside, forty miles north.
pt_BR: Estamos aqui há três dias. O rádio militar morreu ontem. A última transmissão dizia que existe uma zona segura — Riverside, sessenta quilômetros ao norte.

column1: We're heading there at dawn. You're welcome to come. But I need to know — and I need the truth — what happened to your friend Marcus?
en: We're heading there at dawn. You're welcome to come. But I need to know — and I need the truth — what happened to your friend Marcus?
pt_BR: Partimos ao amanhecer. Você pode vir. Mas preciso saber — e preciso da verdade — o que aconteceu com o seu amigo Marcus?

column1: Tell Garcia everything about Marcus
en: Tell Garcia everything about Marcus
pt_BR: Contar tudo ao Garcia sobre o Marcus

column1: Give a vague answer — 'we got separated'
en: Give a vague answer — 'we got separated'
pt_BR: Dar uma resposta vaga — 'nos separamos'

column1: Decline the offer — you travel alone
en: Decline the offer — you travel alone
pt_BR: Recusar a oferta — você viaja sozinho

column1: Good. We leave at 5 AM. Priya handles weapons. Sam runs medical. You and your people handle fuel and watches.
en: Good. We leave at 5 AM. Priya handles weapons. Sam runs medical. You and your people handle fuel and watches.
pt_BR: Bom. Partimos às 5h. Priya cuida das armas. Sam cuida do médico. Você e os seus cuidam do combustível e das vigílias.

column1: About the kid. I've seen bites turn people in six hours. If he turns in the car, I'll put him down. That's not negotiable.
en: About the kid. I've seen bites turn people in six hours. If he turns in the car, I'll put him down. That's not negotiable.
pt_BR: Sobre o garoto. Já vi mordidas transformarem pessoas em seis horas. Se ele virar dentro do carro, eu vou derrubá-lo. Isso não é negociável.

column1: Danny is sitting outside, arm wrapped, pale. He doesn't know what they're saying about him. But he can guess.
en: Danny is sitting outside, arm wrapped, pale. He doesn't know what they're saying about him. But he can guess.
pt_BR: Danny está sentado lá fora, braço enfaixado, pálido. Ele não sabe o que estão dizendo sobre ele. Mas pode imaginar.

column1: Your call. But that road north? It's not forgiving. If you get in trouble, don't come back here.
en: Your call. But that road north? It's not forgiving. If you get in trouble, don't come back here.
pt_BR: Sua decisão. Mas aquela estrada ao norte? Ela não perdoa. Se você se meter em encrenca, não volte aqui.

column1: You fill up the truck and drive north alone. The road is empty. The radio picks up static and fragments — coordinates, warnings, screaming.
en: You fill up the truck and drive north alone. The road is empty. The radio picks up static and fragments — coordinates, warnings, screaming.
pt_BR: Você abastece o caminhão e dirige sozinho para o norte. A estrada está vazia. O rádio capta estática e fragmentos — coordenadas, avisos, gritos.

column1: Forty miles to Riverside. The road is blocked, detoured, and littered with the remains of people who tried to outrun the end.
en: Forty miles to Riverside. The road is blocked, detoured, and littered with the remains of people who tried to outrun the end.
pt_BR: Sessenta quilômetros até Riverside. A estrada está bloqueada, desviada e coberta com os restos de quem tentou fugir do fim.

column1: Somewhere behind you, Garcia's group is either following or fortifying. Somewhere in your backseat, Danny is either sleeping or turning.
en: Somewhere behind you, Garcia's group is either following or fortifying. Somewhere in your backseat, Danny is either sleeping or turning.
pt_BR: Em algum lugar atrás de você, o grupo de Garcia está seguindo você ou se fortificando. Em algum lugar do seu banco de trás, Danny está dormindo ou se transformando.

column1: You'll know soon enough.
en: You'll know soon enough.
pt_BR: Você vai saber logo o suficiente.

column1: Riverside. A walled community. Guard towers. Floodlights. People who look like they've been here long enough to feel safe — and suspicious of anyone who hasn't.
en: Riverside. A walled community. Guard towers. Floodlights. People who look like they've been here long enough to feel safe — and suspicious of anyone who hasn't.
pt_BR: Riverside. Uma comunidade murada. Torres de vigilância. Refletores. Pessoas que parecem estar aqui há tempo suficiente para se sentirem seguras — e desconfiadas de quem não está.

column1: A checkpoint. Medical screening. And a question on every wall, in every guard's eyes: who are you, and what did you do to get here?
en: A checkpoint. Medical screening. And a question on every wall, in every guard's eyes: who are you, and what did you do to get here?
pt_BR: Um posto de controle. Triagem médica. E uma pergunta em cada parede, nos olhos de cada guarda: quem é você, e o que fez para chegar até aqui?

column1: I'm Dr. Chen. Medical screening. I need to check everyone in your vehicle for bites. This is non-negotiable.
en: I'm Dr. Chen. Medical screening. I need to check everyone in your vehicle for bites. This is non-negotiable.
pt_BR: Sou a Dra. Chen. Triagem médica. Preciso verificar todos no seu veículo por mordidas. Isso não é negociável.

column1: If anyone is infected, we can offer them palliative care. We don't turn people away. But we do quarantine. Understand?
en: If anyone is infected, we can offer them palliative care. We don't turn people away. But we do quarantine. Understand?
pt_BR: Se alguém estiver infectado, podemos oferecer cuidados paliativos. Não recusamos ninguém. Mas fazemos quarentena. Entende?

column1: Allow the screening — be honest about Danny
en: Allow the screening — be honest about Danny
pt_BR: Permitir a triagem — ser honesto sobre o Danny

column1: Allow the screening — you have nothing to hide
en: Allow the screening — you have nothing to hide
pt_BR: Permitir a triagem — você não tem nada a esconder

column1: Refuse — you don't trust them
en: Refuse — you don't trust them
pt_BR: Recusar — você não confia neles

column1: The bite is progressing. I'm sorry. He has maybe twelve hours before the fever takes him.
en: The bite is progressing. I'm sorry. He has maybe twelve hours before the fever takes him.
pt_BR: A mordida está progredindo. Sinto muito. Ele tem talvez doze horas antes da febre levá-lo.

column1: We can make him comfortable. And we have been working on something — experimental. No guarantees. It might slow the infection. It might not work at all.
en: We can make him comfortable. And we have been working on something — experimental. No guarantees. It might slow the infection. It might not work at all.
pt_BR: Podemos deixá-lo confortável. E estivemos trabalhando em algo — experimental. Sem garantias. Pode retardar a infecção. Pode não funcionar.

column1: I don't want to turn. Please. I don't want to be one of them.
en: I don't want to turn. Please. I don't want to be one of them.
pt_BR: Eu não quero virar. Por favor. Não quero ser um deles.

column1: Dr. Chen waits. Danny waits. The clock is the only thing that doesn't.
en: Dr. Chen waits. Danny waits. The clock is the only thing that doesn't.
pt_BR: Dra. Chen espera. Danny espera. O relógio é a única coisa que não espera.

column1: Let Danny try the experimental treatment
en: Let Danny try the experimental treatment
pt_BR: Deixar Danny tentar o tratamento experimental

column1: Just make him comfortable — let him go peacefully
en: Just make him comfortable — let him go peacefully
pt_BR: Só deixá-lo confortável — deixá-lo partir em paz

column1: Spend his last hours with him
en: Spend his last hours with him
pt_BR: Passar as últimas horas com ele

column1: The treatment is brutal. Danny screams. His fever spikes. Then, slowly, it breaks.
en: The treatment is brutal. Danny screams. His fever spikes. Then, slowly, it breaks.
pt_BR: O tratamento é brutal. Danny grita. A febre dispara. Então, lentamente, cede.

column1: His vitals are stabilizing. I don't believe it. The infection is retreating.
en: His vitals are stabilizing. I don't believe it. The infection is retreating.
pt_BR: Os sinais vitais estão estabilizando. Não acredito. A infecção está recuando.

column1: Did it work? I feel... I feel okay. I actually feel okay.
en: Did it work? I feel... I feel okay. I actually feel okay.
pt_BR: Funcionou? Eu sinto... eu me sinto bem. Eu me sinto bem mesmo.

column1: You sit with Danny. He talks about his dad. About the dog. About a girl named Sofia he never got the nerve to talk to.
en: You sit with Danny. He talks about his dad. About the dog. About a girl named Sofia he never got the nerve to talk to.
pt_BR: Você senta com Danny. Ele fala do pai. Do cachorro. De uma garota chamada Sofia com quem nunca teve coragem de falar.

column1: You were the last good thing that happened to me. I want you to know that.
en: You were the last good thing that happened to me. I want you to know that.
pt_BR: Você foi a última coisa boa que me aconteceu. Quero que você saiba disso.

column1: At 3:47 AM — the same time everything started — Danny closes his eyes. He doesn't open them again.
en: At 3:47 AM — the same time everything started — Danny closes his eyes. He doesn't open them again.
pt_BR: Às 3h47 da manhã — a mesma hora em que tudo começou — Danny fecha os olhos. Ele não os abre de novo.

column1: You spend the last hours talking. About everything and nothing. He teaches you how to do a card trick. You teach him how to hotwire a car.
en: You spend the last hours talking. About everything and nothing. He teaches you how to do a card trick. You teach him how to hotwire a car.
pt_BR: Vocês passam as últimas horas conversando. Sobre tudo e sobre nada. Ele te ensina um truque de cartas. Você ensina a dar partida num carro sem chave.

column1: If you find Sofia — her last name is Marchetti, she goes to Lincoln High — tell her I should have said something. That I was an idiot.
en: If you find Sofia — her last name is Marchetti, she goes to Lincoln High — tell her I should have said something. That I was an idiot.
pt_BR: Se você encontrar a Sofia — o sobrenome dela é Marchetti, ela estuda no Lincoln High — diga que eu devia ter falado algo. Que eu fui um idiota.

column1: He turns at dawn. Dr. Chen handles it. You don't watch. But you hear it.
en: He turns at dawn. Dr. Chen handles it. You don't watch. But you hear it.
pt_BR: Ele se transforma ao amanhecer. A Dra. Chen cuida disso. Você não olha. Mas ouve.

column1: Then you can't come in. I'm sorry. The rules exist for a reason.
en: Then you can't come in. I'm sorry. The rules exist for a reason.
pt_BR: Então vocês não podem entrar. Sinto muito. As regras existem por um motivo.

column1: You sit in the truck outside the walls. Night falls. The sounds come closer.
en: You sit in the truck outside the walls. Night falls. The sounds come closer.
pt_BR: Você senta no caminhão fora dos muros. A noite cai. Os sons se aproximam.

column1: They come at midnight. A horde. Dozens. Maybe a hundred. Drawn by the lights of Riverside. The gates hold — for now.
en: They come at midnight. A horde. Dozens. Maybe a hundred. Drawn by the lights of Riverside. The gates hold — for now.
pt_BR: Eles vêm à meia-noite. Uma horda. Dezenas. Talvez cem. Atraídos pelas luzes de Riverside. Os portões aguentam — por enquanto.

column1: You're outside the gates. The truck is running. You have seconds.
en: You're outside the gates. The truck is running. You have seconds.
pt_BR: Você está fora dos portões. O caminhão está ligado. Você tem segundos.

column1: Drive away — you don't owe these people anything
en: Drive away — you don't owe these people anything
pt_BR: Dirigir para longe — você não deve nada a essa gente

column1: Fight alongside Riverside — sound the horn, draw the horde
en: Fight alongside Riverside — sound the horn, draw the horde
pt_BR: Lutar ao lado de Riverside — buzinar, atrair a horda

column1: Use the chaos to sneak inside the walls
en: Use the chaos to sneak inside the walls
pt_BR: Usar o caos para entrar escondido pelos muros

column1: Riverside takes you in. It's not much — a cot, a meal, walls that hold. But it's more than most people have.
en: Riverside takes you in. It's not much — a cot, a meal, walls that hold. But it's more than most people have.
pt_BR: Riverside te acolhe. Não é muito — uma maca, uma refeição, muros que aguentam. Mas é mais do que a maioria tem.

column1: Weeks pass. You find a role. You find a rhythm. And then you find the radio message.
en: Weeks pass. You find a role. You find a rhythm. And then you find the radio message.
pt_BR: Semanas passam. Você encontra um papel. Encontra um ritmo. E então encontra a mensagem de rádio.

column1: [RADIO]: ...calling any survivors. Military convoy en route to Riverside. 48 hours. If you can hear this, hold on. Help is coming. Repeat...
en: [RADIO]: ...calling any survivors. Military convoy en route to Riverside. 48 hours. If you can hear this, hold on. Help is coming. Repeat...
pt_BR: [RÁDIO]: ...chamando quaisquer sobreviventes. Comboio militar a caminho de Riverside. 48 horas. Se podem ouvir isso, aguente. Ajuda está vindo. Repetindo...

column1: The horde comes before the convoy. Two thousand strong, drawn by something — sound, smell, or just the instinct to destroy what's alive.
en: The horde comes before the convoy. Two thousand strong, drawn by something — sound, smell, or just the instinct to destroy what's alive.
pt_BR: A horda chega antes do comboio. Dois mil fortes, atraídos por algo — som, cheiro, ou apenas o instinto de destruir o que está vivo.

column1: We can hold the gate for an hour. Maybe two. If we evacuate through the north tunnel, we lose the settlement but we live.
en: We can hold the gate for an hour. Maybe two. If we evacuate through the north tunnel, we lose the settlement but we live.
pt_BR: Podemos segurar o portão por uma hora. Talvez duas. Se evacuarmos pelo túnel ao norte, perdemos o assentamento, mas vivemos.

column1: This is it. Everything you did — who you saved, who you abandoned, who you let in, who you left behind — it all comes down to this.
en: This is it. Everything you did — who you saved, who you abandoned, who you let in, who you left behind — it all comes down to this.
pt_BR: É isso. Tudo o que você fez — quem salvou, quem abandonou, quem deixou entrar, quem deixou para trás — tudo se resume a isto.

column1: Hold the gate — buy time for everyone to evacuate
en: Hold the gate — buy time for everyone to evacuate
pt_BR: Segurar o portão — ganhar tempo para todos evacuarem

column1: Evacuate immediately — save who you can
en: Evacuate immediately — save who you can
pt_BR: Evacuar imediatamente — salvar quem puder

column1: Draw the horde away from Riverside — alone
en: Draw the horde away from Riverside — alone
pt_BR: Atrair a horda para longe de Riverside — sozinho

column1: Steal a vehicle and leave — let them sort it out
en: Steal a vehicle and leave — let them sort it out
pt_BR: Roubar um veículo e ir embora — deixar que eles se resolvam

column1: Tell Dr. Chen to release the experimental cure — risk it all
en: Tell Dr. Chen to release the experimental cure — risk it all
pt_BR: Pedir à Dra. Chen que libere o tratamento experimental — arriscar tudo

column1: Keep your head down and stay silent — let the walls hold or fall without you
en: Keep your head down and stay silent — let the walls hold or fall without you
pt_BR: Manter a cabeça baixa e ficar em silêncio — deixar que os muros aguentem ou caiam sem você

column1: You held the gate for three hours. When the convoy arrived, they found you slumped against the barricade, still breathing, still you.
en: You held the gate for three hours. When the convoy arrived, they found you slumped against the barricade, still breathing, still you.
pt_BR: Você segurou o portão por três horas. Quando o comboio chegou, encontraram você caído contra a barricada, ainda respirando, ainda você.

column1: Riverside survived because you bought them the time they needed. The convoy took you in. The bite on your arm healed. Nobody knows why.
en: Riverside survived because you bought them the time they needed. The convoy took you in. The bite on your arm healed. Nobody knows why.
pt_BR: Riverside sobreviveu porque você comprou o tempo de que precisavam. O comboio te acolheu. A mordida no seu braço cicatrizou. Ninguém sabe por quê.

column1: Some people say it's because you did enough good to earn a second chance. Maybe. Or maybe the world just isn't done with you yet.
en: Some people say it's because you did enough good to earn a second chance. Maybe. Or maybe the world just isn't done with you yet.
pt_BR: Alguns dizem que é porque você fez bem o suficiente para merecer uma segunda chance. Talvez. Ou talvez o mundo simplesmente não tenha terminado com você.

column1: You evacuated 87 people through the north tunnel. Riverside fell, but the people didn't.
en: You evacuated 87 people through the north tunnel. Riverside fell, but the people didn't.
pt_BR: Você evacuou 87 pessoas pelo túnel ao norte. Riverside caiu, mas o povo não.

column1: The convoy found you on the road two days later. A caravan of survivors and a story about someone who made the hard call at the right time.
en: The convoy found you on the road two days later. A caravan of survivors and a story about someone who made the hard call at the right time.
pt_BR: O comboio te encontrou na estrada dois dias depois. Uma caravana de sobreviventes e a história de alguém que tomou a decisão difícil na hora certa.

column1: You survived. You'll have to decide if that's enough.
en: You survived. You'll have to decide if that's enough.
pt_BR: Você sobreviveu. Vai ter que decidir se isso é suficiente.

column1: You took the truck and drove south, horn blaring, radio screaming. The horde followed you. All of them.
en: You took the truck and drove south, horn blaring, radio screaming. The horde followed you. All of them.
pt_BR: Você pegou o caminhão e dirigiu para o sul, buzinando, rádio gritando. A horda te seguiu. Todos eles.

column1: Riverside never knew what you did. The convoy arrived to a settlement that was untouched. They found the truck three miles south, empty, doors open.
en: Riverside never knew what you did. The convoy arrived to a settlement that was untouched. They found the truck three miles south, empty, doors open.
pt_BR: Riverside nunca soube o que você fez. O comboio chegou a um assentamento intocado. Encontraram o caminhão a cinco quilômetros ao sul, vazio, portas abertas.

column1: They never found you. But Riverside lives. And that was the point.
en: They never found you. But Riverside lives. And that was the point.
pt_BR: Nunca te encontraram. Mas Riverside vive. E esse era o objetivo.

column1: You drove. The radio said the convoy was coming. You didn't turn back.
en: You drove. The radio said the convoy was coming. You didn't turn back.
pt_BR: Você dirigiu. O rádio dizia que o comboio estava vindo. Você não voltou.

column1: Weeks later, you hear that Riverside fell. Everyone. The convoy was too late. You don't know if that's your fault. You'll spend the rest of your life deciding.
en: Weeks later, you hear that Riverside fell. Everyone. The convoy was too late. You don't know if that's your fault. You'll spend the rest of your life deciding.
pt_BR: Semanas depois, você ouve que Riverside caiu. Todos. O comboio chegou tarde demais. Você não sabe se é culpa sua. Vai passar o resto da vida decidindo.

column1: The road goes on. So do you. Alone.
en: The road goes on. So do you. Alone.
pt_BR: A estrada continua. E você também. Sozinho.

column1: You slipped through the north gate during the chaos. Nobody saw you come in. Nobody cared.
en: You slipped through the north gate during the chaos. Nobody saw you come in. Nobody cared.
pt_BR: Você entrou pelo portão norte durante o caos. Ninguém viu você entrar. Ninguém se importou.

column1: Riverside fell that night. You survived by hiding in a storm drain while the screaming lasted six hours.
en: Riverside fell that night. You survived by hiding in a storm drain while the screaming lasted six hours.
pt_BR: Riverside caiu naquela noite. Você sobreviveu se escondendo num bueiro enquanto os gritos duraram seis horas.

column1: The convoy found you the next day. They asked what happened. You said you didn't know. They believed you. You wish you didn't.
en: The convoy found you the next day. They asked what happened. You said you didn't know. They believed you. You wish you didn't.
pt_BR: O comboio te encontrou no dia seguinte. Perguntaram o que aconteceu. Você disse que não sabia. Eles acreditaram. Você queria que não acreditassem.

column1: Dr. Chen administered the experimental treatment to everyone — infected, exposed, everyone. The fever broke. The gray skin receded. The dead became... less dead.
en: Dr. Chen administered the experimental treatment to everyone — infected, exposed, everyone. The fever broke. The gray skin receded. The dead became... less dead.
pt_BR: A Dra. Chen aplicou o tratamento experimental em todos — infectados, expostos, todos. A febre cedeu. A pele cinza recuou. Os mortos se tornaram... menos mortos.

column1: It wasn't a cure. Not really. But it was a chance. And in the first winter of the end, a chance was everything.
en: It wasn't a cure. Not really. But it was a chance. And in the first winter of the end, a chance was everything.
pt_BR: Não era uma cura. Não exatamente. Mas era uma chance. E no primeiro inverno do fim, uma chance era tudo.

column1: Danny was the key. His blood had something we'd never seen. If you hadn't brought him here... none of this would exist.
en: Danny was the key. His blood had something we'd never seen. If you hadn't brought him here... none of this would exist.
pt_BR: Danny foi a chave. O sangue dele tinha algo que nunca tínhamos visto. Se você não o tivesse trazido aqui... nada disso existiria.

column1: You saved the kid. The kid saved everyone. The dead hours are ending.
en: You saved the kid. The kid saved everyone. The dead hours are ending.
pt_BR: Você salvou o garoto. O garoto salvou todos. As horas mortas estão terminando.

column1: You made it through. Riverside took you in, eventually. You got a cot, a job, a routine.
en: You made it through. Riverside took you in, eventually. You got a cot, a job, a routine.
pt_BR: Você conseguiu. Riverside te acolheu, eventualmente. Você ganhou uma maca, um trabalho, uma rotina.

column1: But you never told anyone about the voice at the door. The kid you left on the curb. The friend you let in when you shouldn't have.
en: But you never told anyone about the voice at the door. The kid you left on the curb. The friend you let in when you shouldn't have.
pt_BR: Mas você nunca contou a ninguém sobre a voz na porta. O garoto que deixou na calçada. O amigo que deixou entrar quando não devia.

column1: The dead walk outside the walls. But some of the dead walk inside them too. The ones you carry.
en: The dead walk outside the walls. But some of the dead walk inside them too. The ones you carry.
pt_BR: Os mortos andam fora dos muros. Mas alguns mortos andam dentro deles também. Aqueles que você carrega.

column1: He will use it, if he has to. Don't give him a reason.
en: He will use it, if he has to. Don't give him a reason.
pt_BR: Ele vai atirar, se precisar. Não dê um motivo a ele.

column1: Slow and easy. Hands where I can see them. I've shot three people this week who moved too fast.
en: Slow and easy. Hands where I can see them. I've shot three people this week who moved too fast.
pt_BR: Devagar e com calma. Mãos onde eu possa ver. Atirei em três pessoas esta semana que se moveram rápido demais.

column1: He's right. The kid stays outside the fence. But I'll leave him a blanket. It gets cold.
en: He's right. The kid stays outside the fence. But I'll leave him a blanket. It gets cold.
pt_BR: Ele tem razão. O garoto fica do lado de fora da cerca. Mas vou deixar uma manta para ele. Vai ficar frio.

column1: I used to run a checkpoint outside São Paulo. Two hundred people a day lied to my face. You know what honesty is worth now? Everything.
en: I used to run a checkpoint outside São Paulo. Two hundred people a day lied to my face. You know what honesty is worth now? Everything.
pt_BR: Eu costumava comandar um posto de controle nos arredores de São Paulo. Duzentas pessoas por dia mentiam na minha cara. Sabe quanto vale a honestidade hoje? Tudo.

column1: Nobody travels alone anymore. Nobody. Remember that when you tell us your story later.
en: Nobody travels alone anymore. Nobody. Remember that when you tell us your story later.
pt_BR: Ninguém mais viaja sozinho. Ninguém. Lembre-se disso quando contar sua história mais tarde.

column1: I had a sister who trusted the wrong stranger. I buried what was left of her myself. So no — I don't give warnings twice.
en: I had a sister who trusted the wrong stranger. I buried what was left of her myself. So no — I don't give warnings twice.
pt_BR: Eu tinha uma irmã que confiou no estranho errado. Enterrei o que sobrou dela com as minhas próprias mãos. Então não — eu não aviso duas vezes.

column1: So I'll ask once. What happened to Marcus?
en: So I'll ask once. What happened to Marcus?
pt_BR: Então vou perguntar uma vez. O que aconteceu com o Marcus?

column1: I had fourteen people under my command before all this. Nine made it to this gas station. Four since. Do the math on my patience.
en: I had fourteen people under my command before all this. Nine made it to this gas station. Four since. Do the math on my patience.
pt_BR: Eu tinha quatorze pessoas sob meu comando antes disso tudo. Nove chegaram a este posto. Quatro desde então. Faça as contas da minha paciência.

column1: Kid asked me for water an hour ago. I gave it to him. If he turns, remember I did that too.
en: Kid asked me for water an hour ago. I gave it to him. If he turns, remember I did that too.
pt_BR: O garoto me pediu água uma hora atrás. Eu dei. Se ele virar, lembre que eu fiz isso também.

column1: I'm not a cruel man. I'm a careful one. There's a difference, and out here the difference keeps people breathing.
en: I'm not a cruel man. I'm a careful one. There's a difference, and out here the difference keeps people breathing.
pt_BR: Não sou um homem cruel. Sou um homem cuidadoso. Há uma diferença, e aqui fora a diferença mantém as pessoas respirando.

column1: I've watched people drive off full of pride. None of them came back to gloat. Take the fuel. It's on the house.
en: I've watched people drive off full of pride. None of them came back to gloat. Take the fuel. It's on the house.
pt_BR: Já vi gente partir cheia de orgulho. Nenhum voltou para se gabar. Fique com o combustível. Por conta da casa.

column1: I was an epidemiologist. I spent my whole career preparing for something like this. It didn't help. Maybe you'll be the exception.
en: I was an epidemiologist. I spent my whole career preparing for something like this. It didn't help. Maybe you'll be the exception.
pt_BR: Eu era epidemiologista. Passei a carreira inteira me preparando para algo assim. Não ajudou em nada. Talvez você seja a exceção.

column1: I've watched forty-one people turn. I promised every one of them I'd try. I'm promising you the same thing now.
en: I've watched forty-one people turn. I promised every one of them I'd try. I'm promising you the same thing now.
pt_BR: Eu vi quarenta e uma pessoas se transformarem. Prometi a cada uma que eu tentaria. Estou prometendo a mesma coisa a você agora.

column1: Eleven trials. Eleven failures. I told myself after the last one that I was done experimenting on people. And then your friend walked in.
en: Eleven trials. Eleven failures. I told myself after the last one that I was done experimenting on people. And then your friend walked in.
pt_BR: Onze testes. Onze fracassos. Disse a mim mesma, após o último, que tinha acabado com experimentos em pessoas. E então o seu amigo apareceu.

column1: I hope whatever you're hiding out there is worth the walls you won't enter. Good luck. Truly.
en: I hope whatever you're hiding out there is worth the walls you won't enter. Good luck. Truly.
pt_BR: Espero que o que quer que você esteja escondendo aí fora valha os muros que não vai cruzar. Boa sorte. Sinceramente.

column1: I've given orders in worse places. But never to people I actually care about. Make it count.
en: I've given orders in worse places. But never to people I actually care about. Make it count.
pt_BR: Já dei ordens em lugares piores. Mas nunca a pessoas de quem realmente gosto. Faça valer a pena.

column1: I counted the first wave. We don't have enough ammo to make a dent. Whatever we choose, choose it now.
en: I counted the first wave. We don't have enough ammo to make a dent. Whatever we choose, choose it now.
pt_BR: Contei a primeira onda. Não temos munição suficiente nem para arranhá-los. Seja o que for que vamos escolher, escolha agora.

column1: Forty-one people turned on my watch. This is for them. Every single one of them.
en: Forty-one people turned on my watch. This is for them. Every single one of them.
pt_BR: Quarenta e uma pessoas se transformaram sob meus cuidados. Isso é por elas. Cada uma delas.
